Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD's top-level (global) scope consists only of ordinary variable assignments and array definitions: `pkgname`, `_pkg_git_src`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `optdepends`, `makedepends`, `provides`, `conflicts`, and empty `source=()` / `sha256sums=()` arrays. None of these use command substitution, `eval`, encoded blobs, network calls, or any side-effecting operation that would execute during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. The remaining content is entirely function definitions (`pkgver`, `prepare`, `build`, `package`), which are NOT invoked by `--printsrcinfo` and are therefore out of scope for this gate.

The `source` array is empty, so there is nothing fetched or verified at metadata-parse time anyway. The `prepare()`/`pkgver()`/`build()`/`package()` bodies perform standard git clone/checkout of the package's own upstream (`LibreOffice/dictionaries`), a spase-checkout of `pt_PT`, a `git pull --ff-only`, and routine installs into `$pkgdir`. Those are normal packaging operations and, being inside functions, cannot run during `--printsrcinfo`. As a hygiene note for the later full audit: the source is unpinned (tracks `master` and does a build-time `git pull --ff-only`), which weakens reproducibility, and `makedepends` pulls the large `qt6-webengine` — neither is a security defect in this parsing step.

No top-level code executes a downloaded payload or exfiltrates data. Running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` on this file is safe.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Only top-level variable/array/function definitions; no execution on parse.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard `.SRCINFO` metadata file generated by `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. It contains only package metadata for `hunspell-pt_pt-git`: description, version, architecture, licenses, and dependency declarations. There is no executable code, no shell commands, no network requests, no obfuscation, and no file operations whatsoever.

The declared upstream URL (`https://github.com/LibreOffice/dictionaries/tree/master/pt_PT`) points to the well-known, legitimate LibreOffice dictionaries repository, which is the appropriate upstream for a Portuguese hunspell dictionary. Dependencies (`git`, `qt6-webengine`) and conflicts/provides entries are ordinary and consistent with the package's stated purpose. Nothing deviates from normal packaging practices.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard SRCINFO metadata only; no code or suspicious content.</summary>
</security_assessment>

[1/2] Reviewing PKGBUILD...
+ Reviewed .SRCINFO. Status: SAFE -- Standard SRCINFO metadata only; no code or suspicious content.
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD packages European Portuguese hunspell dictionaries. It declares `source=()` and `sha256sums=()` and instead clones the upstream dictionary repository in `prepare()` via `git clone`, sparse checkout of `pt_PT`, `git checkout master`, then `git pull --ff-only`. The remote (`https://github.com/LibreOffice/dictionaries.git`) is exactly the project's declared upstream (matching `url=`), so this is the package's own source being fetched, not an unrelated host.

The `git pull --ff-only` in `prepare()` does pull unchecked content from a mutable branch (`master`) at build time, which weakens reproducibility and widens the supply-chain window. This is a hygiene/reproducibility concern worth noting, but the pulled content is only dictionary text files built into a `.bdic` via `qwebengine_convert_dict` and installed into `$pkgdir` — it is not executed, and there are no other red flags.

No obfuscated/encoded content, no `eval`/`base64`/`curl|bash`, no exfiltration of local data, and no modifications outside `$pkgdir`/`$srcdir`. The remaining steps (`install`, symlinks under `/usr/share/myspell`, license/doc install) are standard packaging. Overall, consistent with ordinary AUR practice for a `-git` dictionary package.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard -git dictionary PKGBUILD; only unpinned upstream pull noted, no malice.</summary>
</security_assessment>
